# Calendar Requirements Readiness Checklist: Calendar / Takvim

**Purpose**: Review requirements completeness, clarity, consistency, and implementability for SPEC-007's Calendar read semantics, navigation, offline boundary, authorization, ownership, accessibility, and exclusions.
**Created**: 2026-10-06
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are eligible tasks explicitly limited to unfinished work in ACTIVE seasons with an approved plan, consistently across spec and planning artifacts? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002; Plan §Architecture and Data Flow]
- [ ] CHK002 Are overdue tasks specified as a separate attention group, with overdue derived from the unchanged original planned date? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004–006]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the selected-date agenda explicitly limited to that Business-local date, while keeping overdue tasks separate for every selected date? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004–007]
- [ ] CHK004 Are completed tasks excluded from Calendar while completion/history ownership remains with SPEC-003 and SPEC-006? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, FR-020–021]
- [ ] CHK005 Are Field scope defaults and optional narrowing consistently defined for agenda and month indicators, with authorization remaining server-side? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK006 Does the month view remain a work-presence overview on original planned dates plus date navigation, without becoming a task-list or redefining dates? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008–009]

## Requirement Clarity and Consistency

- [ ] CHK007 Are canonical task eligibility, the overdue group, selected-date tasks, and month indicators defined as one coherent Calendar result with consistent Field scope? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002–010; Plan §Architecture and Data Flow]
- [ ] CHK008 Are cursor semantics defined to bind authorization scope and every result-defining query parameter, including date/month, Field, and task group? [Completeness, Plan §API Contract Direction; Contract §POST /v1/calendar/reads and GET /v1/calendar/reads/{readId}/pages]
- [ ] CHK009 Do the artifacts define how a shared read identity prevents concurrent inserts, completions, or other task-state changes across overdue pages, selected-date pages, and month indicators from causing skipped/duplicated rows or false completeness? [Gap, Plan §API Contract Direction; Contract §CalendarReadResult]
- [ ] CHK010 Is “complete saved view” defined to require every task page and month-indicator component for the exact selected date and Field scope, with month indicators alone explicitly insufficient for another date's task rows? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016–018; Plan §Saved Calendar Read Model]
- [ ] CHK011 Are the planning artifacts consistent about whether saved task coverage is exact-date or full-month task coverage? [Consistency, Research §Bound month indicators and paginate task groups; Plan §Saved Calendar Read Model; Data Model §Validation and invariants]
- [ ] CHK012 Are retryable connectivity failures, explicit authentication/authorization denials, and known authorization loss distinguished clearly enough to govern fallback eligibility? [Coverage, Spec §FR-015–018; Contract §responses]
- [ ] CHK013 Are account and server-resolved Business partitioning, Field narrowing, non-disclosing out-of-scope behavior, and the rule that cached data never grants authority clearly specified? [Security, Spec §FR-010, FR-016–018; Plan §Saved Calendar Read Model]

## Scenario and Edge-Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK014 Are no ACTIVE season, no unfinished work, and no work for a selected Field defined as distinct informational empty states without setup actions? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014; Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK015 Are loading, recoverable/retryable error, unavailable, empty, and saved/offline states distinguishable, including behavior when no complete matching snapshot exists? [Coverage, Spec §FR-016–019]
- [ ] CHK016 Are date changes, Field changes, out-of-coverage selections, interrupted pagination, request races, account changes, Business changes, and access-denial cases covered without partial display or speculative merging? [Coverage, Spec §FR-016–018; Plan §Request Races and State]
- [ ] CHK017 Are task detail contents and read-only boundaries explicit, preserving task/date context without absorbing Today execution or History/Diary behavior? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012–013, FR-020]

## Non-Functional Requirements and Scope Boundaries

- [ ] CHK018 Are accessibility semantics specified for date selection, Field filtering, task rows, month work indicators, overdue status, and loading/error/empty/saved announcements without mandating visual styling? [Accessibility, Spec §FR-019; Plan §Accessibility and Interaction Architecture]
- [ ] CHK019 Are the boundaries against DRAFT work, completed tasks, task mutations, weather proposals, Season filters, backlogs, setup actions, generic sync, auth leases, reminders, finance, harvest/sales, team/advisor, and AI explicit across the artifacts? [Scope, Spec §FR-022; Scope Boundaries]
- [ ] CHK020 Are Today, History/Diary, and Season setup/activation ownership preserved without duplicated execution, history, or DRAFT-planning behavior in Calendar? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014, FR-020–022]

## Reviewer Assessment (requirements quality only)

This assessment records the requested review; checklist markers above remain unchecked for reviewer ownership.

| Result | Items |
|---|---|
| Pass | CHK001–020 |
| Fail | None |

### Findings

- **Resolved — CHK009 (High)**: `plan.md`, `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `calendar.openapi.yaml`, and `quickstart.md` now define a Calendar-specific PostgreSQL `REPEATABLE READ` read snapshot, identity dimensions, immutable task/day projections, stable key ordering, recorded server-issued cursors, current authorization revalidation, concurrency behavior, chain validation, complete-view promotion, expiry, and restart behavior. No generic snapshot/read platform is introduced.
- **Resolved — CHK011 (Medium)**: All planning artifacts now state that month indicators cover month-level presence only, while task-row coverage is limited to the exact selected date plus the complete overdue group. A different selected date requires its own complete saved view; month indicators do not permit task-row fallback for that date. No full-month task prefetch is specified.

## Implementation Readiness Evidence (2026-10-06)

- Calendar scope/acceptance review found no code-to-spec contradiction across navigation ownership, server-authoritative Business-local dates, ACTIVE/approved/unfinished eligibility, immutable pagination, current authorization checks, Field scope, offline completeness, or mutation exclusions.
- Exact disposable database verification and both PostgreSQL integration suites passed on `ekim_hasat_test`; final full mobile verification passed 41 suites / 240 tests. Repository API/domain tests passed (API 156/156; domain 95/95), and generated-client/API contract verification passed 63/63.
- Impeccable invocation was reconciled to the Codex skill workflow in `.agents/skills/impeccable/SKILL.md` and its references; the bundled executable is a detector/hook and maintenance CLI, not a command runner for `shape`, `critique`, `audit`, or `polish`. The Main Agent completed shape, critique/audit (single-context, explicitly degraded per repository agent policy), refinement, and polish workflows. The deterministic Calendar markup scan returned no findings. Source audit scores: accessibility 3/4, performance 3/4, appearance/theming 1/4, platform conformance 3/4, adaptivity 3/4 (13/20). Calendar's selected Field value and selected-date paging label were refined and the automated accessibility suite passes. Light-only hard-coded colors and potential long-list render cost remain documented follow-up risks; a feature-only theme change would diverge from the app's current light-only surfaces. Physical-device and VoiceOver/TalkBack runtime checks were not performed and are deferred, not PASS.
- API aggregate-runner diagnosis: the sandbox run failed only the two Calendar HTTP-bound suites, whose direct run reported `listen EPERM: operation not permitted 127.0.0.1`. The unchanged aggregate passed 156/156 when rerun with approved loopback access; root API/domain tests and the client/API contract aggregate also passed. This was an environment permission failure, not an API implementation or parallel-test defect; no timeout, worker count, test order, DB configuration, or test semantics were changed.
